overview:
This check collects the number of CPU cores on a host and CPU times, such as `system`, `user`, `idle`, etc.

**Minimum Agent version:** 6.0.0
setup:
### Installation

The System Core check is included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package. No additional installation is needed on your server.

### Configuration

1. Edit the `system_core.d/conf.yaml` file in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your [Agent's configuration directory][3]. See the [sample system_core.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options. **Note**: At least one entry is required under `instances` to enable the check, for example:

   ```yaml
   init_config:

   instances:
     - foo: bar
   ```

2. [Restart the Agent][5].

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][6] and look for `system_core` under the Checks section.

[2]: /account/settings/agent/latest
[3]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/guide/agent-configuration-files/#agent-configuration-directory
[4]: https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/system_core/datadog_checks/system_core/data/conf.yaml.example
[5]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/guide/agent-commands/#start-stop-and-restart-the-agent
[6]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/guide/agent-commands/#agent-status-and-information
troubleshooting:
Need help? Contact [Datadog support][9].

### Windows and high numbers of processors

Due to [the way Windows splits processors into groups][10], metrics
for individual cores collected from this integration may have invalid
values for Windows hosts with high (> 64) numbers of cores for a
portion of the cores.

Note that `*.total` metrics should still reflect accurate values in
the above situation, and only per-core metrics are affected.

Datadog recommends that users with this type of configuration set up the
[Windows Performance Counters integration][11] to track counters
inside the `Processor Information`. This enables users to get accurate per-core
metrics.

[9]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/help/
[10]: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/processor-groups
[11]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/windows_performance_counters/

metrics.name: system.core.count
metrics.description: The number of CPU cores on the host

metrics.name: system.core.user
metrics.description: The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent in user mode

metrics.name: system.core.user.total
metrics.description: The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent in user mode

metrics.name: system.core.system
metrics.description: The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent in kernel mode

metrics.name: system.core.system.total
metrics.description: The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent in kernel mode

metrics.name: system.core.idle
metrics.description: The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent idle

metrics.name: system.core.idle.total
metrics.description: The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent idle

metrics.name: system.core.nice
metrics.description: [Unix] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent in niced (prioritized) processes in user mode

metrics.name: system.core.nice.total
metrics.description: [Unix] The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent in niced (prioritized) processes in user mode

metrics.name: system.core.guest
metrics.description: [Linux] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent running a virtual CPU for guest operating systems under the control of the Linux kernel

metrics.name: system.core.guest.total
metrics.description: [Linux] The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent running a virtual CPU for guest operating systems under the control of the Linux kernel

metrics.name: system.core.iowait
metrics.description: [Linux] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent waiting for I/O to complete

metrics.name: system.core.iowait.total
metrics.description: [Linux] The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent waiting for I/O to complete

metrics.name: system.core.irq
metrics.description: [Linux, BSD] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent servicing hardware interrupts

metrics.name: system.core.irq.total
metrics.description: [Linux, BSD] The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent servicing hardware interrupts

metrics.name: system.core.softirq
metrics.description: [Linux, BSD] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent servicing software interrupts

metrics.name: system.core.softirq.total
metrics.description: [Linux, BSD] The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent servicing software interrupts

metrics.name: system.core.guest_nice
metrics.description: [Linux] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent running a niced guest

metrics.name: system.core.guest_nice.total
metrics.description: [Linux] The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent running running a niced guest

metrics.name: system.core.steal
metrics.description: [Linux] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent running a virtual CPU for guest operating systems under the control of the Linux kernel

metrics.name: system.core.steal.total
metrics.description: [Linux] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent running a virtual CPU for guest operating systems under the control of the Linux kernel

metrics.name: system.core.interrupt
metrics.description: [Windows] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent servicing hardware interrupts

metrics.name: system.core.interrupt.total
metrics.description: [Windows] The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent servicing hardware interrupts

metrics.name: system.core.dpc
metrics.description: [Windows] The percentage of time a given CPU core has spent servicing deferred procedure calls (DPCs)

metrics.name: system.core.dpc.total
metrics.description: [Windows] The percentage of time the whole CPU has spent servicing deferred procedure calls (DPCs)

metrics.name: system.core.frequency
metrics.description: The frequency or clock speed a given CPU
